html:
The 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso, born Lhamo Thondup in 1935, is the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism and the head of its Gelug school. He has lived in exile in India since 1959.

He was born to a farming family in Amdo, in northeastern Tibet. Monks searching for the rebirth of the 13th Dalai Lama identified him as a small child, and he was formally recognised in 1939 and brought to Lhasa. The title of Dalai Lama goes back to 1578, and since the time of the 5th Dalai Lama its holders had also ruled Tibet.

His life turned on the arrival of Chinese rule:

  • 1950: the army of the new People's Republic of China entered Tibet, and he took up political power at fifteen.
  • 1950s: he tried to work with Beijing and met Mao Zedong.
  • 1959: after the Tibetan uprising in Lhasa was crushed, he fled to India. Tens of thousands of Tibetans followed him into exile.
  • From 1960: he led the Tibetan government in exile from Dharamshala in India.
  • 1989: he won the Nobel Peace Prize for his non-violent campaign for Tibet.
  • 2011: he handed his political role to an elected leader.

He has asked for real autonomy for Tibet within China rather than independence, which he calls the Middle Way. Beijing calls him a separatist and claims the right to approve his successor.

Abroad he became one of the best-known religious figures in the world, writing and speaking about compassion, Buddhism and science.
